Evan M: Heads-up: onboarding repo sample fails on Windows with python 3.11 in venv, SSL verify error when calling the SDK.
Rhea S: Can you paste the exact error?
Evan M: 
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:997)
```
Evan M: Env: Win10, python.org 3.11.2, venv, redwood-sdk 0.7.0. Works on our linux dev boxes.
Rhea S: Did you try certifi + SSL_CERT_FILE? Windows cert store sometimes not picked up by embedded OpenSSL in wheels.
Evan M: Yep, setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() fixes it. But this is rough for new users.
QA-Lead: Flagging as onboarding pain — can we add an automated check in the sample to detect Windows+venv and print a hint?
Rhea S: SDK fix idea: accept ssl_context on both sync and async clients and prefer env SSL_CERT_FILE -> certifi -> system. Also update type stubs so AsyncClient signature remains typed.
Evan M: Agree. Also add a short Quickstart note and a debugging command to print openssl version and cert path.
DevExBot: Created ticket INF-3499: "py-sdk: windows venv cert precedence & async ssl_context" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3499 :white_check_mark:
Rhea S: I'll open a small PR to expose ssl_context param and fallback order, include mypy/typing updates. Ping QE when draft ready for Win 3.8-3.12 matrix.
Evan M: Thanks — that should smooth new-hire setup. Leaving thread until docs + patch are released.
